lawyer:
Shamsuddin Babul with Golam Kibria Advocates—For the Petitioner.
Fahima Nasrin, Advocate—For the Respondent No.4 Ahmed Sohel, Advocate—For the respondent Nos. 1 and 2.
parties:
Saidul Haque Shamim (Md) ------- Petitioner
Vs.
Anti-Corruption Commission and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Farah Mahbub J: In this Rule, issued under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, the respondents have been called upon to show cause as to why the impugned Memo No. 1606 dated 29-9-2009 issued by the respondent No. 1 under the signature of respondent No. 2 asking the petitioner to appear before him for recording statement in connection with Gulshan Police Station Case No. 111 dated 30-5-2009 (Annexure-D) and also as to why entertainment/investigation of the said Police Station Case corresponding to GR No. 618/2009 under section 408 of the Penal Code now, pending in the Court of respondent No. 3 should not he declared to have been made without lawful authority and hence, of no legal effect 

 2. Facts, in brief, are that one Md Ali Asgar Quarishi being the Chairman of Multi Residential Systems Ltd incorporated under the Companies Act, 1994 as well as the Managing Director of Mukti Manoshik and Madakashakti Niamey Kendra Ltd. lodged an FIR (First Information Report) on 30-5-2009 with Gulshan Police Station bearing No.111 (5)09 implicating the petitioner and another under section 408 of the Penal Code. It has been stated further that on receipt of the said FIR the duty officer of Gulshan Police Station, DMP Dhaka having registered the case forwarded the same to the Officer-in-Charge of the said police station for necessary steps regarding investigation. Accordingly, the Officer-in-Charge of the said police station had entrusted the case to one Sub-Inspector Abul Bashar, on the same date i.e., 30-5-2009 for investigation. 

 3. On receipt of summons of the aforesaid case, the petitioner voluntarily surrendered before the court concern and obtained bail from the concerned court below vide order dated 2-6-2009 (Annexure-B). The cause of action arose on 20-9-2009 when the respondent No. 1 under the signature of respondent No. 2 being allegedly influenced by the informant of the case, most illegally and arbitrarily and with a view to harass the petitioner issued the impugned order dated 29-9-2009 directing him to appear before for recording his statements in connection with Gulshan Police Station Case No 111 dated 30-5-2009, as registered under section 408 of the Penal Code. 

 5. Mr Shamsuddin Babul appearing with Mr Golam Kibria, the learned Advocates for the petitioner submits upon placing rule 4 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 (in short, the Rules) that vide the said provision the Anti-Corruption Commission (in short, ACC) is empowered to take information into account which was sent to it by the respective police station within 2(two) days of receipt thereof. But in the instant case, as it is apparent from the order sheet that the FIR was not forwarded to the ACC in compliance of the said provision i.e., it has not been sent within 2 (two) days from the date of receipt thereof, for consideration and investigation; rather, it was registered as GR No. 618 of 2009 and had proceeded accordingly appointing one Sub-Inspector of the said police station for investigation of the allegation so made against the petitioner and another. Accordingly, he submits that issuance of the impugned notice by the respondent No.2 directing him to appear before the Commission with supporting documents to assist the investigation in connection with the said GR case, is without jurisdiction and hence, it is liable to be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority. He further goes to argue that as per section 19 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Ain, 2004 (in short, the Ain) the Commission is authorised to investigate any schedule offence and thereupon the investigating authority on conclusion of investigation shall submit report to the Commission under rule 10 of the Rules, 2007; whereupon sanction will be given by the Commission with a view to file the case under rule 30 of the said Rules. He also submits that there is no provision either in the Act of 2004 or Rules, 2007 to interfere or takeover or withdraw any case which was filed and registered as GR case and investigate the same within the periphery of the Act of 2004. In that view of the Smatter as well, he submits that issuance of the impugned notice by the respondent No. 2 should be knocked down for violation of the provisions as incorporated in the Anti-Corruption Commission Ain, 2004 as well as the Rules, 2007. 

 6. Mr Ahmed Sohel, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of Anti-Corruption Commission by producing the respective office file in connection with the instant case submits that it is apparent therefrom that though the FIR has been lodged with the respective Police Station but in compliance of rule 4 of the Rules of 2007 the same was not forwarded to the Commission within the prescribed period of 2(two) days. In this connection referring to the ratio as decided in ACC vs Dr Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir reported in 62 DLR (AD) 290 he submits that to that effect the Appellate Division has categorically observed particularly at para 31 that "Rules 3 and 4 of the Rules provides only for filing of the complaint involving the offences mentioned in the schedule to the Act. However, those provisions are merely directory and deviation from provisions in lodging an First Information Report instead of a complaint would not vitiate the proceedings." In other words, he submits that for not sending the First Information Report to the Commission for the purpose of investigation within the said prescribed period of time cannot go to vitiate the entire proceedings, for the same is merely directory. He also submits by referring to the rationale of Md Habib Abdur Rab vs State, in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.4042 of 2009 that vide the judgment and order dated 07-11-2012 one of the Benches of this Division has categorically found that offence under section 408 of the Penal Code being a schedule offence. has to be investigated by the Commission in view of the provisions as enumerated in section 20 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Ain, 2004- as such, the investigation so has been initiated by one Sub-Inspector of Gulshan Police Station has no mandate of law. 

 7. In the present Rule Nisi the main contention of the petitioner is that in view of rule -4 of the "দুর্নীতি দমন কমিশন বিধিমালা (in short, the Rules) the information so lodged with the concerned police station since has not been for-warded within the prescribed period of time i.e., within 2 days of receipt thereof, rather upon registering the case as GR No.618 of 2009 it proceeded under the Code of Criminal Procedure (in short, the Code) hence, issuance of the impugned order by the Investigating Officer of the Commission directing the petitioner to appear before the Commission with supporting documents to assist the investigation, is without jurisdiction. 

 12. In the instant case, Gulshan Police Station Case No. 111(5) of 2009 corresponding to GR No.618 of 2009 has been lodged by the informant under section 408 of the Penal Code for the alleged misappropriation of money. As per clause (ga) of the schedule of the Act offence under section 408 of the Penal Code is a schedule offence. In this regard section 20 of the Act provides as under— 

 13. In view of the said provision it is only the Commission which shall investigate the schedule offence and submit report thereof; however, the case shall be tried under section 28(2) of the Act, 2004; which is quoted below: - 

 "Lodging FIR in respect of corruption in police station—Notwithstanding anything contained in these rules, there shall be no bar to lodge FIR complaint in the police station in respect of offence mentioned in the schedule of the Act, provided that the police station concerned shall upon receipt of the complaint enter it in the Register and send within two working days, the same to the nearest District office in the case of officers and employees outside the Commission and to the Commission in the case of officers and employees of the Commission, for investigation." 

 16. In the instant case, on receipt of the complaint on 30-5-2000 it had been registered as Gulshan Police Station Case No111(5)2009. On perusal of the record of the Anti-Corruption Commission (as placed before us for perusal) it appears that in compliance of rule 4 of the Rules, 2007 the FIR has not been sent to the Commission for investigation within the said prescribed period of time. However, vide Memo No. অপরাধ/৩৪৬০/ডিসি (গুলশান বিভাগ) dated 3-6-2009 the Deputy Police Commissioner (Gulshan Division), Gulshan had forwarded an office letter addressing the Police Commissioner, Dhaka Metropolitan Police, Dhaka with a prayer to send the case record to the Anti-Corruption Commission for investigation. Pursuant thereto the Joint Police Commissioner (Crime and Operation) on behalf of the Commissioner vide Memo No. ডিএমপি(সঃদঃ)/অপরাধ/দুদক/১২-২০০৯/গুলশান-১/৮০০২ dated 8-6-2009 had requested the Secretary, Anti-Corruption Commission to take necessary steps for investigation of the matter in question contending, inter alia, that the case had been lodged under section 408 of the Penal Code which was a schedule offence of the Act of 2004. Ultimately, vide Memo No. দুদক/স জে কা/ঢাক-১/১৪৫৬/১(৩) dated 19-8-2009 one Md Akther Hossain, a Deputy Director of the Commission had been deputed as the Investigating Officer to conduct the investigation of the case in question. 

 "In the instant case, an officer of the Commission lodged a first Information report on 6-3-2007 with the Tejgaon Police Station and a case was started. This is not envisaged under rules 3 and 4 of the Rules. Those rules provided only for filing of the complaint involving the offences mentioned in the schedule to the Act. However, those provisions are merely directory and deviation from provisions in lodging an first information report instead of a complaint, would not vitiate the proceedings."
